summary: The freeze is repaired the right way: the subject now matches its dispatched digest, and its size and mtime are unchanged from the failed dispatch, so the coordinator re-measured rather than rewriting — the turn-3 content was never what was in question. On the merits everything holds. The third edit Codex's ADV-D093-T2-01 required is present, and it repairs something I missed at turn 2: the live DR-105 cell carried the stale v2 claim a second time, in a later sentence my finding never reached. The two DR-105 targets are disjoint and each unique, so the same cell can take both edits without collision, and the v1 REJECT history, the 7-blocker join, the DR-G09 and BLK remainders and the not-SATISFIED sentence all survive untouched. Both of my turn-2 notes were restored.

selfCorrection.whatIDid: At turn 1 I read the DR-105 cell in full and printed it, and my finding was that the entry's own replacement text restated 'a permission v2 successor' as owed when D-042 had already recorded v2. That was correct and necessary. At turn 2 I verified the entry had removed the claim from its prose and its replacement, and had imported D-042's remaining-unmet list, and I consented.
selfCorrection.whatIMissed: The printout I generated at turn 1 contained the sentence 'D-032 dispositions that join; a permission v2 successor and the host-effect contract remain.' — a second, independent instance of the same false claim, later in the same cell, which none of the entry's edits touched. So after the turn-2 write the register would still have asserted the very thing my MUST-FIX was about. My finding was right in direction and incomplete in scope.
selfCorrection.theDisciplineIFailedToApply: When an entry restates a stale claim, sweep the whole target cell for other instances of that claim rather than stopping at the one the entry reproduces. I applied exactly that discipline two entries earlier — at D-088 I swept the entire register for every statement depending on the zero-named-harness value, and at D-092 I traced the stale G17 route into a second cell. Here I had the cell's full text on screen and did not re-read it for repeats of the claim I was objecting to.
selfCorrection.whyItMattersBeyondThisEntry: The two failures have the same shape as the ADV-D056-01 lesson: verify what an instrument displaces, not only what it does. The extension I am recording for myself is narrower and more mechanical — after identifying a false or stale claim, grep the target cell for the claim's distinguishing terms before reporting, because a cell can carry the same assertion in more than one sentence and a replacement aimed at one leaves the other standing.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. Two things belong on the record. First, the freeze failure was repaired the honest way: the file is byte-for-byte what it was when the first dispatch failed, so the digest was corrected to the bytes rather than the bytes rewritten to the digest, which is what makes this a re-dispatch rather than a fourth turn. Second, this turn corrects me. Codex's ADV-D093-T2-01 found that the DR-105 cell asserted the permission-v2 falsehood twice, and my turn-1 MUST-FIX reached only the instance the entry reproduced — I had the full cell text in front of me and did not sweep it for repeats of the claim I was objecting to. My finding was right in direction and short in scope, and I have recorded the narrower discipline it teaches. What lands now is better than what I asked for: three disjoint unique edits, the false claim removed from both places it lived, and the v1 REJECT history, the seven-blocker join and the row's not-SATISFIED sentence all left standing.
